paragraphs: The CLS 320 was part of the original CLS range from 2004, spanning two generations: the C219 (2004-2010) and the C218 (2010-2018). The first-generation C219 used a choice of V6 engines - the M112 or M272 petrol units, or the OM642 diesel in some markets (though diesel variants were more commonly badged as CLS 350d from the C218 onward). From the C218 generation, the CLS 320 petrol continued with the M272, while diesel versions used the OM642. The CLS was discontinued entirely after the C257 in 2023 - no successor exists, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLS 320 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre or 3.5-litre V6 petrol engine fitted to the earliest C219-generation CLS 320 from 2004 to 2006. No specific known issue has been independently confirmed for this engine in this application. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M112 rebuild.

A 3.0-litre or 3.5-litre V6 petrol engine fitted to the CLS 320 from approximately 2006 onwards, across both C219 and C218 generations. No specific known issue has been independently confirmed for this engine in this application. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M272 rebuild.

A 3.0-litre V6 diesel engine, badged as the CLS 350d from the C218 generation onward. This engine is known for swirl flap and injector wear - see the callout above. We replace swirl flaps, injector seals and the timing chain as standard on every OM642 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLS 320 spans multiple engine codes across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an M272 part will work on an M112 or OM642 car - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLS quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
